questions.question:
**Select the correct option:**

The journalist refused to ___ her sources despite repeated legal threats.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. give out .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The journalist refused to reveal her sources. The correct phrasal verb here is **"give out"**, which means to disclose or release information.
 
• Each of the options has a specific meaning:
 
 
• **Give out:** To disclose or share information.
 
• **Give over:** To hand over or stop doing something (doesn’t fit here).
 
• **Give away:** To reveal a secret or give something for free (not entirely suitable in this context).
 
• **Give up:** To surrender or stop doing something (does not fit here).
 
 
 
• Therefore, "give out" is the most appropriate choice.

Correct sentence: *The journalist refused to **give out** her sources despite repeated legal threats.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Select the correct option:**

The memorandum clarified that employees must comply ___ the revised code of ethics.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. **with**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition **with** is commonly used after the verb **comply** to indicate adherence or obedience to rules, regulations, or standards.
 
• The sentence refers to compliance with the revised code of ethics, so **with** is the appropriate choice.
 
• Other options such as **to, by,** or **in** are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Correct sentence: *The memorandum clarified that employees must comply **with** the revised code of ethics.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of prepositions:**
 
 
• **Comply with:** To follow rules or adhere to standards. Example: "You must comply with the safety regulations."
 
• **Comply to:** Incorrect usage; avoid using "to" after comply.
 
• **Comply by:** Rarely used and usually incorrect in this context.
 
• **Comply in:** Incorrect usage; "in" does not fit grammatically here.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Change the following from active to passive: **

The jury has delivered a unanimous verdict.

options.text: A unanimous verdict has been delivered by the jury.
A unanimous verdict was being delivered by the jury.
A unanimous verdict had been delivered by the jury.
A unanimous verdict is delivered by the jury.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. A unanimous verdict has been delivered by the jury. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To change a sentence from active to passive voice, the subject becomes the receiver of the action, and the object becomes the doer.
 
• The active sentence here is: **The jury has delivered a unanimous verdict.**
 
• In passive voice, the object ("a unanimous verdict") comes first, followed by the verb in the passive form. The subject ("the jury") follows, preceded by "by".
 
• The correct passive construction is: **A unanimous verdict has been delivered by the jury.**

Correct sentence: *A unanimous verdict has been delivered by the jury.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active voice:** The subject performs the action expressed by the verb.
 
 
• **Example:** The chef prepared the meal.
 
 
 
• **Passive voice:** The subject receives the action expressed by the verb.
 
 
• **Example:** The meal was prepared by the chef.
 
 
 
• Verb tense in passive voice is formed by using the correct form of "to be" + the past participle of the main verb.
</ul

questions.question:
**Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:**

The construction is alleged to have been halted due to environmental violations.

options.text: It is alleged that the authorities halted the construction.
The authorities are alleged to have halted the construction.
The violation allegedly halted the construction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. **The authorities are alleged to have halted the construction.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **passive voice**, where the subject receives the action.
 
• To convert it to the **active voice**, the focus shifts to the performer of the action (i.e., the authorities).
 
• Among the options provided, Option 3 accurately conveys the meaning of the original sentence in active voice.
 
• Option 3, "The authorities are alleged to have halted the construction," maintains the context of the allegation and specifies who performed the action.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Passive Voice Structure:** Subject + verb (to be) + past participle + additional information.
 
• **Active Voice Structure:** Subject (performer of action) + verb + object + additional information.
 
• In this case, the authorities are the subject performing the action, making Option 3 the most appropriate active voice transformation.

• **Direct Speech:** "I had completed the report." becomes **Indirect Speech:** "She said that she had completed the report."
 
• **Tense Change:**
 
 
• Past perfect tense ("had completed") remains unchanged in indirect speech because it is already in the correct form.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The pronoun "I" in direct speech is changed to "she" in indirect speech to match the subject of the reporting verb "she said."
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" remains as it is in indirect speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The sentence is introduced with "that" to link the reporting clause and the reported speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *She said that she had completed the report.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She said that she completed the report."
 
 
• Incorrect because the past perfect tense ("had completed") is not maintained, which changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "She said that she has completed the report."
 
 
• Incorrect because the present perfect tense ("has completed") is used, which does not align with the past perfect tense of the direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said she had been completing the report."
 
 
• Incorrect because the past perfect continuous tense ("had been completing") changes the meaning of the original sentence, implying an ongoing action rather than a completed action.
